(a) Computation of Retired Pay.—The table in section 1401(a) of title 10, United States Code, is amended—
        (1) in the column designated “Column 2”, by inserting “, not to exceed 75%,” after “percentage of disability” both places it appears; and 
        (2) by striking column 4.  
    (b) Recomputation of Retired or Retainer Pay to Reflect Later Active Duty of Members Who First Became Members Before September 8, 1980.—The table in section 1402(d) of such title is amended—
        (1) in the column designated “Column 2”, by inserting “, not to exceed 75%,” after “percentage of disability”; and 
        (2) by striking column 4.  
    (c) Recomputation of Retired or Retainer Pay to Reflect Later Active Duty of Members Who First Became Members After September 7, 1980.—The table in section 1402a(d) of such title is amended—
        (1) in the column designated “Column 2”, by inserting “, not to exceed 75 percent,” after “percentage of disability”; and 
        (2) by striking column 4.  
    (d) Application of Amendments.—The tables in sections 1401(a), 1402(d), and 1402a(d) of title 10, United States Code, as in effect on the day before the date of the enactment of this Act, shall continue to apply to the computation or recomputation of retired or retainer pay for persons who first became entitled to retired or retainer pay under subtitle A of such title on or before the date of the enactment of this Act. The amendments made by this section shall apply only with respect to persons who first become entitled to retired or retainer pay under such subtitle after that date.

fable.w: This section only makes technical amendments to the tables used to compute and recompute military retired or retainer pay, and sets which persons the amendments apply to. It involves no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. There is no tempting opposite reading, because nothing in the text touches on an outside party taking part in a federal decision.

opus.w: This section only amends the retired pay tables in 10 U.S.C. 1401 and 1402: it caps the disability percentage at 75% and strikes column 4. It also sets which retirees the new rules cover. Nothing in it has the federal government consult or coordinate with anyone outside the government. Mentions of people entitled to retired pay describe who gets the benefit, not anyone taking part in a federal decision.
opus.b: 1. **Reasoning.** The only tempting reading comes from words like "entitled to retired or retainer pay" and "persons," which might suggest outside parties taking part. That reading fails. The section only changes the formulas in the military retired pay tables and says which people the new formulas apply to. There's no comment period, rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, consultation or right to sue. Eligibility for benefits isn't participation anyway.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends statutory tables used to compute retired pay for military members. It does not require any consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties (such as the public, states, or non-federal experts) before the decision is made. The changes are purely administrative and mathematical adjustments to benefit calculations for federal employees.
qwen_chat.s: (a) Computation of Retired Pay.—The table in section 1401(a) of title 10, United States Code, is amended— (1) in the column designated “Column 2”, by inserting “, not to exceed 75%,” after “percentage of disability” both places it appears; and (2) by striking column 4.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the section affects military members (who are individuals), it involves participation. However, military members are federal employees/insiders, and this section merely changes the mathematical formula for their pay. It does not require them to consult, comment, or participate in the decision-making process; it simply dictates how their benefits are calculated.
